use_when: To let the user opt in to something, such as marketing emails or staying signed in.
To confirm the user has read and agreed to terms before they continue, such as the booking terms or cancellation policy.
To make the user acknowledge a destructive action before it runs, using the error state (for example, "I understand this is permanent").
For a list of options where the user can choose any number, such as search filters.

dont_use_when.when: For a setting that takes effect immediately: use the Toggle component instead.
When the user must pick exactly one option from a list: use the Radiocard component instead.
To trigger an action: use the Button component instead.

variant_intent.checked: The tick shows the checked state, so it doesn't rely on colour alone.

a11y.fact: The control is a native <input type="checkbox">, so keyboard, focus and disabled behaviour are the browser's own.
The input and label text sit inside one <label>, so clicking the label text toggles the checkbox and gives it its accessible name.
The tick is a decorative SVG hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden); the checked state is carried by the native input.
